related_questions.question: How long are you contagious with COVID after testing positive?
related_questions.snippet: While people become less contagious over time, they are still contagious with COVID for an average of eight days. That may vary depending on factors including underlying health conditions and the severity of illness.
related_questions.title: How Long Am I Contagious? - Yale New Haven Hospital

related_questions.question: What is the best thing to take to reduce COVID symptoms?
related_questions.snippet: Take an over-the-counter medicine such as acetaminophen or ibuprofen. These can be used as a fever reducer or to treat headache, sore throat or body aches. While ibuprofen will reduce your fever, there is some concern that it may not be safe to take with the novel coronavirus.
related_questions.title: COVID Treatment at Home - University of Maryland Medical System

related_questions.question: How long do I need to isolate with COVID?
related_questions.snippet: For the first time since 2021, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has updated its COVID isolation guidance. Specifically, it has shifted the recommendation that someone who tests positive for COVID isolate for five days to a timeline based on the progression of the person's symptoms.
related_questions.title: Virologist Explains the CDC's New COVID Isolation Guidance

related_questions.question: Why didn't I get COVID from my spouse?
related_questions.snippet: If you've been vaccinated or had a prior infection, your immune system could be able to knock out the pathogen.
related_questions.title: My partner/roommate/kid got COVID. And I didn't. How come? - NPR
